mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20d returns in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60d returns in more than 60% of quarters when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 0.4 percentage points for three consecutive months signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > previous month + 0.4pp for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20d returns in more than 50% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO of more than 0.5% signals deteriorating industrial production, which foreshadows lower corporate revenues and earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 20d returns in more than 40% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which depresses corporate earnings and equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 5d returns in more than 50% of such co-declining months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 yields positive 60d returns in more than 40% of such dual-trigger episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in PAYEMS above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12mo moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20d returns in more than 50% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in RSAFS above its 6-month average signals rising household savings, which may reflect precautionary behavior and weaker consumption, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days in any macro regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 20d returns in more than 60% of months when RSAFS is above its 6-month average.
